main_diagnosis: The `forward` function in `SimulatorStep` is completely unimplemented — it contains only a placeholder (`...`) and returns the unchanged state. This means the simulator produces zero dynamics, explaining the catastrophically large NLE scores (~4.36e+30). The entire SIR stochastic transition logic is missing.

issues.description: The `forward` method body is empty (only `...` and `next_state = state.copy()`). No SIR epidemic dynamics are computed, so every predicted next state equals the current state, making the likelihood of any real trajectory essentially zero and producing astronomically bad NLE metrics.
issues.suggestion: Implement the discrete stochastic SIR dynamics using the two parameters: `beta = parameters[0]` (transmission rate) and `gamma = parameters[1]` (recovery rate). Compute `N = S + I + R`, then draw new infections as `new_infections = rng.binomial(S, 1 - np.exp(-beta * I / N))` and new recoveries as `new_recoveries = rng.binomial(I, gamma)`. Clamp values so they stay non-negative. Return `{'S': S - new_infections, 'I': I + new_infections - new_recoveries, 'R': R + new_recoveries}`. This matches a standard discrete-time stochastic SIR model and is both interpretable and a faithful approximation of the continuous ODE.

issues.description: The `parameters` attribute is never initialised in `__init__`, so calling `get_parameters()` before `set_parameters()` will raise an `AttributeError`. Additionally, there are no default or prior-reasonable initial values (e.g., beta~0.3, gamma~0.1) to fall back on.
issues.suggestion: In `__init__`, add `self.parameters = np.array([0.3, 0.1])` (sensible COVID-19 defaults: beta≈0.3, gamma≈0.1) so the simulator is usable immediately after construction without requiring an explicit `set_parameters` call first.
